description: A `packages/cli-core` usage check across scenarios flags any scenario whose CLI does not follow the canonical pattern, surfacing findings as warnings in validation output.

requirements.description: The `cli-health validate <scenario>` command (and optionally a standalone audit sub-command) must inspect each scenario's CLI entry point to verify it uses the canonical `packages/cli-core` pattern. Scenarios whose CLI does not import or delegate to `cli-core` in the expected manner must produce a warning-level finding with code NON_CANONICAL_CLI_PATTERN, including the scenario name and the detected pattern deviation. These findings must not fail validation (exit code remains 0) but must appear in the validation output.
requirements.title: Non-Canonical CLI Pattern Detection Across Scenarios

validation.notes: Given a scenario CLI entry point that does not import cli-core, validate returns NON_CANONICAL_CLI_PATTERN at warning severity
Given a scenario CLI entry point that correctly uses cli-core, validate returns zero NON_CANONICAL_CLI_PATTERN findings
Given a NON_CANONICAL_CLI_PATTERN warning and no error-level findings, exit code is 0
Run `cli-health validate` across all 6 adopting scenarios; assert all pass (exit 0) and any NON_CANONICAL_CLI_PATTERN warnings are reported for non-conformant scenarios
Introduce a synthetic scenario with a hand-rolled CLI bypassing cli-core; assert NON_CANONICAL_CLI_PATTERN warning is produced
Enforcing the canonical CLI pattern ensures consistent behaviour, flag parsing, and error formatting across all scenario CLIs

title: Non-canonical CLI pattern detection
